title: ORE-TASTE-01 — I Don't Know What It Tastes Like

cards.text: ORE-TASTE-01 — I DON'T KNOW WHAT IT TASTES LIKE

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: MOF creator-to-camera, ~41s, one unbroken take, preorder window. Answers the taste question by refusing to answer it, which is the only legal move (no samples exist, taste gate unpassed, 16 CFR 255.1). Traced beat-for-beat off the Apothekary Blue Burn TikTok Shop comment-reply. Golden nugget: the taste she is scared of is the one she already lives with. FORCED BREAK FROM REFERENCE: the reference holds the product 40s; ours legally cannot, so she holds HER OWN children's chewable bottle instead, frame one to last. Every Orelli visual is an asset-pack cut-in added in post.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The comments don't lie.
Front cam, mirrored, chest-up CU, bathroom. Product already in hand at chest height. Native reply-comment sticker top-left. Bold outlined all-caps card low-mid frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Flat verdict. Settling an argument.

BOOKEND LINE. The same line closes the ad.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The zero appetite and the craving water like crazy is real.
Same static frame. Free hand points at lens. Comment sticker still up.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Validating the commenter.

Answers the specific claim in the sticker.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: These are the Apothekary Blue Burn drops.
Sticker drops out, product-name card comes up.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Plain naming.

Product named at 5.6s, not before.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And like I said, what it's gonna do, get them sides touching... ready for summertime in no time.
No text card. Hands come together on 'sides touching'.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Building, gesture-led.

Outcome stack. Ours becomes the flat spec beat.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: This right here is gonna boost that metabolism... buying a new pair of pants because the other ones do not fit, and I mean it.
Longest beat, 10.7s. Thumbs up, then points directly at lens.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Peak energy, escalating image.

The long persuasion run. Ours becomes the golden nugget.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I went and had me a nice steak dinner, couldn't eat any of it.
Same frame, smaller gestures. Story mode.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Drops into anecdote.

Personal proof moment begins.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Probably ate maybe a quarter of it, and I was so full, and I was mad at these drops, but I knew it was working.
Points at the bottle on 'these drops'.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Self-deprecating, then conviction.

THE TWIST beat. Highest-leverage moment in the reference. Ours becomes the checkout line.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So like I said... hit the orange cart 'cause the drops do work and the comments don't lie.
Points to product, then to lens. Music fades.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Back to flat conviction.

CTA + bookend echo.

cards.title: REFERENCE CREATIVE — Apothekary Blue Burn (TikTok Shop, 40.6s)  ·  tiktok 7633948921462525197 / o_m_briii
SCRIPT
cards.text: "I don't know what it tastes like."

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Front cam, arm's length, chest-up. Real bathroom or parked car. HER OWN children's chewable bottle already in hand at chest height, LABEL TURNED AWAY. Real comment sticker top-left. #ad card top-right.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Flat. No wink. It should sound like the opposite of an ad.

NON-NEGOTIABLE word for word. NO ORELLI PRODUCT IN ANY FILMED FRAME. Not held, not opened, not received. 16 CFR 255.1.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: "Every comment asks the same thing, so I'm gonna be straight with you."

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Static. Small shrug, direct to lens. Comment sticker still up.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Direct. Settling it, not selling.

COMMENT STICKER MUST BE REAL, pulled off our own content. Nobody authors one. If none exists, flag before shoot day.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: "It's called Orelli and it doesn't ship till December."

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: No cut-in yet. Plain delivery.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Flat, no lift.

Pronounce it or-RELL-ee. Say CHEWABLE, never gummy or soft chew (7/30 Brooks law; conflicts with the affiliate sheet, flagged to Brooks).

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: "It's a chewable. Five hundred milligrams, same active ingredient as Extra Strength Tylenol. No water, nothing to swallow."

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: POST CUT-IN: side-by-side comparison card, overlay reads 'Same active ingredient. 500mg.' Then single-chew hero over her shoulder. Card: 500MG. SAME ACTIVE INGREDIENT.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Matter of fact. Spec, not pitch.

'Same active ingredient as Tylenol' is explicitly allowed and encouraged. 'Better/stronger/faster than' is banned. Comparison asset was flagged for legal review; if uncleared, fall back to a plain 500mg text card.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: "Here's what I do know. I'm thirty-one and there's a bottle of children's grape chewables in my cabinet right now. Before that I crushed pills into applesauce. So everybody keeps asking if it's gonna taste bad. I already know what bad tastes like."

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: She lifts the bottle already in her hand on 'children's grape chewables'. First time the viewer learns why it has been there for 14 seconds. Card: I'M 31 AND I BUY THE KIDS ONES.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
The one place she warms up. Real age, real cabinet.

THE GOLDEN NUGGET. The taste she is scared of is the one she already lives with. This is the beat that lets the ad address taste without ever claiming a flavor.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: "I bought those in a checkout line last month."

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Small nod at the bottle in her hand. Energy drops.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Quiet. Setting up the story.

HER STORY, not ours. If the checkout moment never happened to her, she swaps in the one that did and tells us what she changed.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: "The woman ringing me up asked how old my kid was. I said thirty-one. She laughed. So did I, in the car, kind of."

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: No cut-in. Stay on her face. Nothing moves.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Underplayed. Do NOT perform the sadness. The 'kind of' is the whole beat.

The adult-shame payoff. This is the mirror of the reference's steak-dinner twist and it is the highest-leverage moment in the ad.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: "So no, I can't tell you how it tastes yet. It ships December 2026, I preordered, link's in my comments. Ask me in December."

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: POST CUT-IN: add-to-cart tap-through or preorder page with ship date visible. Card: PREORDER · SHIPS DECEMBER 2026.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Back to flat. Same read as line 1.

'I preordered' STAYS ONLY IF SHE ACTUALLY DID. Preorder before posting or cut the two words. Ship date is spoken here and carded, so disclosure is covered twice. Never 'get yours now', 'in stock', 'selling out'.

cards.title: OUR VERSION — ORE-TASTE-01 (shoot ~41s, one take)  ·  Orelli Adult Chewable Acetaminophen · preorder

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: NO ORELLI ON SET
cards.text: No holding, eating, opening, or receiving. No unboxing, no 'look what came in the mail'. Every Orelli visual is an asset-pack cut-in added in post and must read as a picture of a thing that exists, never a thing in her house.

cards.title: SHE HAS NOT TRIED IT
cards.text: Nobody has, including the founders. No 'it tastes like candy', no 'it works', no 'my new go-to'. Announcement, never review. Fines run to $51,744 per violation and land on the creator too.

cards.title: WHAT'S IN HER HAND
cards.text: Her own children's chewable pain reliever, from the first frame to the last, label turned away or brand-free. Never put down. That bottle does the work the product normally does in this shot.

cards.title: CLAIMS CAP
cards.text: The label allows exactly two: temporarily relieves minor aches and pains, temporarily reduces fever. This script deliberately makes neither, which is cleaner. No pregnancy, no kids' dosing, no dosing advice, no interactions, no doctor.

cards.title: DISCLOSURE, ALL THREE
cards.text: #ad in the FIRST LINE of the caption before the cutoff, #ad visible on screen in the first seconds, and TikTok's branded-content toggle on. Link and code in the PINNED comment, actually pinned.

cards.title: PREORDER TERMS
cards.text: Caption must read: Preorder, ships December 2026. Cancel anytime before shipping for a full refund. 'Ships December 2026' also spoken in line 8 and carded at 35s.

cards.title: THE COMMENT ANSWER
cards.text: If someone asks in comments whether it tastes good, the only allowed reply: 'No idea yet honestly, it doesn't ship till December. I preordered because I finally found something I can actually take.'

cards.title: CASTING + LOOK
cards.text: One woman 25-34 who genuinely cannot swallow pills and can evidence it. Bare face, claw clip, bathroom or car, phone mic. Full glam reads as an ad and kills this angle. Room tone only, no music bed.

cards.title: ALT HOOKS — capture all 3
cards.text:
6s each, same setup, no camera move. Each runs into line 2 as written.

A (hero): I don't know what it tastes like.
B: I'm not going to tell you it tastes good. I haven't tried it.
C: I'm thirty-one and I buy the children's medicine. That's the whole video.

cards.title: DELIVERY
cards.text: Raw, ungraded, uncropped, no burned captions, no music, no product cut-ins. 1080x1920, 30fps, front camera. Plus the real comment screenshot at full res, plus a one-line note on what she changed in beats 5-7 to make them true.

cards.title: OPEN FLAG — gummy vs chewable
cards.text: Affiliate compliance sheet allows 'as a gummy' as a format description. Brooks's 7/30 founder-content law says never 'gummy' in any script. Written as CHEWABLE throughout pending his call.

cards.title: OPEN FLAG — taste gate
cards.text: The Oct 15 taste-gate deadline and the refund-everything contingency are deliberately NOT in this script. Strong beat, but making that promise public is Brooks's call.
